status: research only; no rules or suites changed; no scans (the detection-test subset for the separate Flask .jinja change is running in the background)
headline: The JS rules are strongest on Express/Koa/Nest request fields into the classic sinks (SQL, shell, fs, redirect, SSRF, HTML). The measured weakness is not one missing sink: it is framework coverage (Hono/Elysia/tRPC/GraphQL/WebSocket/serverless), archive extraction, a few library-specific sinks (js-yaml, error messages, dynamic res.render), and the front-end DOM shapes already listed in frontend-dom-xss-2026-11-03.json. The JS CVE suite has only 10 cases and 2 finds; the next ground-truth batch matters more than another rule tweak.
method: Read catalog/codewatch/rules/javascript-{taint,injection,web,crypto}.yml and extracted every taint source/sink and the pattern rules.
Read the JS CVE results (2/10 verdict, 4/10 review) and the blind-app notes in README.md/PLAN.md.
Cross-checked the front-end inventory (benchmarks/frontend-dom-xss-2026-11-03.json) for DOM/XSS gaps; no new scans.

gaps.evidence: the shared source set names req/request/ctx/ctx.request/context.req; no Hono c.req, Elysia body/query/params, tRPC input, GraphQL args, AWS Lambda/Vercel event.*, WebSocket/ws message data, or Fastify reply/request decorators beyond the bare names
gaps.proposal: add one source anchor per framework (Hono c.req.query/param/json, Elysia handler destructuring, tRPC input, GraphQL resolver args, serverless event.body/queryStringParameters/pathParameters, ws/socket message handlers). Add only with a non-blind case or an ordinary-app check; each is a broad source and can raise false alarms.
gaps.test: a Hono/Elysia/tRPC/Lambda/WebSocket handler passing its request value to innerHTML or fs; safe: a constant or a parsed/validated value
gaps.risk: broad; start with the framework's explicit request accessor, not every function parameter

gaps.evidence: the path-traversal rule covers fs but no tar/zip library; an archive entry name can escape the extraction directory (zip slip) before any fs call. Python has a tar-extraction hotspot; JS does not.
gaps.proposal: new hotspot codewatch.js.archive-extraction for tar.x/extract, adm-zip extractAllTo, unzipper, yauzl, extract-zip, node-stream-zip, decompress; flag extraction without a member-path check. Review-only: many libraries sanitize or the archive is trusted.
gaps.test: a route extracting an uploaded zip with a '../' entry; safe: an entry-name containment check or a trusted archive
gaps.risk: archive libraries differ; a pattern hotspot is safer than a taint rule

gaps.evidence: GHSA-fh64-r2vc-xvhr (MLflow UI, .tsx) is in cve-pairs-python-frontend: js-yaml load() on an MLmodel artifact can execute custom JS types; the JS unsafe-deserialization rule only names node-serialize/funcster. The fix uses safeLoad.
gaps.proposal: add yaml.load(...)/jsyaml.load(...)/safeLoad? safeLoad is safe; load is unsafe in js-yaml 3 with the default schema, while js-yaml 4 load is safe unless a schema/types option is passed. Add a review hotspot for yaml.load($DATA) (not safeLoad) with a version caveat, or a taint rule when the request value reaches load.
gaps.test: a route parsing request text with yaml.load; safe: yaml.safeLoad or JSON.parse
gaps.risk: js-yaml 4 makes load safe; a verdict rule would false-alarm on modern code. Keep it a hotspot/document the version.

gaps.evidence: the JS stack-trace rule only catches $ERR.stack. err.message, err.toString(), res.json({error: err}) and a caught exception object sent to the client are not covered; Python has a broader exception-message hotspot (CWE-209).
gaps.proposal: add $ERR.message/$ERR.toString() and an error object inside a JSON response as sinks of a new JS exception-message hotspot; do not flag a generic string from the server.
gaps.risk: development handlers often include messages; that is the point of the hotspot

gaps.evidence: res.render($VIEW) is not a sink; a request-controlled view name selects a template outside the intended directory (path traversal/LFI, and SSTI depending on the engine). The template-injection rule catches a request-controlled template string, not the view name.
gaps.proposal: add a path-traversal sink for $RES.render($VIEW, ...) where $VIEW is request data; safe: a literal view name or an allowlisted map.
gaps.risk: view names are often constants; only tainted values

gaps.evidence: SQL sinks cover $DB.query/raw/execute, $queryRawUnsafe/$executeRawUnsafe and Sequelize.literal; Sequelize whereRaw/orderByRaw/havingRaw/where(Sequelize.literal(...)) and Knex whereRaw/orderByRaw are not in the sink list (knex.raw matches $DB.raw).
gaps.proposal: add $MODEL.whereRaw/orderByRaw/havingRaw and $QUERY.whereRaw/orderByRaw, and Knex whereRaw/orderByRaw, with the request value as the tainted argument.
gaps.test: Model.findAll({where: sequelize.whereRaw('name = ' + req.query.name)}) and knex('t').whereRaw('x=' + req.query.x); safe: bound replacements
gaps.risk: the raw method name is explicit; low ambiguity

gaps.evidence: codewatch.js.nosql-injection sources are only $REQ.body/$REQ.query; it misses req.params, destructured body fields, request getters and ctx.query/ctx.request.body in its narrow set (the shared js-sources already has them).
gaps.proposal: give the NoSQL rule the shared *js-sources, or add the missing field names/destructuring; keep the MongoDB $where and collection-method sinks.
gaps.test: const {filter}=req.body; db.collection.find(filter); safe: String(filter.q) or an allowlisted key
gaps.risk: low; this is source consistency, not a new pattern

gaps.evidence: the JS XSS rule does not include React's dangerouslySetInnerHTML; JSX text/{value} is escaped by React and should stay quiet.
gaps.proposal: add a sink for dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html: $HTML}}; DOMPurify.sanitize already sanitizes.
gaps.risk: low if limited to the explicit dangerous prop

gaps.evidence:
the XSS rule covers .html and .append only. GHSA-x7mf (OctoPrint) builds $('

'+value+'

'); GHSA-fmqq (Indico) passes {html: message} to a jQuery dialog.
gaps.proposal: add .prepend/.before/.after/.replaceWith/.wrap/.wrapInner/.appendTo/.prependTo/.insertAfter/.insertBefore/.replaceAll, tainted $('<...>' + value), and dialog({html: value}); .text/createElement stays safe.
gaps.risk: $() is also a selector; require a tainted interpolation, not a plain selector

gaps.evidence: codewatch.js.prototype-pollution-merge only matches a user-written recursive merge function. _.merge({}, req.body), deepmerge, Object.assign (covered as mass assignment, CWE-915), and object-path style setters are not CWE-1321 findings.
gaps.proposal: add a hotspot for _.merge/deepmerge/merge/_.set with a request body as the source, or rely on mass-assignment; do not duplicate the Object.assign finding.
gaps.test: _.merge(target, req.body) with a __proto__ key; safe: a key allowlist or Object.create(null)
gaps.risk: many merges are intentional; review hotspot

gaps.evidence: six .svelte-only fixes are pending (five Open WebUI, one Fava); .vue is a scored extension but no analyzer parses it. A bare {@html}/v-html hotspot flags the fixed files that keep the sink and add DOMPurify.
gaps.proposal: add .svelte to SOURCE_EXTENSIONS['python-web']; add a sanitizer-aware Svelte/Vue rule (see frontend-dom-xss-2026-11-03.json), not a bare hotspot.
gaps.test: {@html error} vs {@html DOMPurify.sanitize(x)}; v-html="trusted" vs a sanitized value

gaps.evidence: the source set is Express/Koa/Nest; AWS Lambda (event.body, event.queryStringParameters, event.pathParameters), Vercel/Next serverless, WebSocket (message/data on ws/socket/io) and Socket.IO handlers are not sources.
gaps.proposal: add explicit event/message sources per framework after a non-blind case; keep them narrow to the handler's first argument/event fields.
gaps.test: exports.handler = (event) => db.query(event.body.q); ws.on('message', data => el.innerHTML = data)
gaps.risk: broad; add with a case and an ordinary-app check

gaps.evidence: the JS CVE suite is 10 cases (2 found, 0 still flagged); the blind JS sets are spent and JS false alarms were the worst (13 in one Express app). The Python pool is exhausted under the current rule; the JS/npm pool is not.
gaps.proposal: collect a JS/Node CVE batch from OSV's npm export with the same acceptance rule (GitHub-reviewed, one fix commit, app code, request-to-sink flow, small focused fix), read each diff, split blind by sha256, and hand back a JSON/TSV. Target Express/Koa/Fastify/Next/Nest app code, not framework/library internals.
gaps.test: the new suite cases drive the next JS rules; the nightly measures them on the main PC.
gaps.risk: the npm pool is large; the reading limit is the same as the Python batches.

next_research: 1. JavaScript/Node CVE ground truth (OSV npm export) is the highest-value next step; it feeds every gap above with evidence instead of hypotheses.
2. Add the evidence-backed sinks with existing cases: js-yaml (GHSA-fh64), jQuery/dialog/DOM shapes, dynamic res.render, error messages.
3. Add framework sources only after a non-blind case; Hono/Elysia/tRPC/GraphQL/serverless/WebSocket are broad and need app checks.
4. Keep the six .svelte pairs pending until a sanitizer-aware Svelte/Vue rule and .svelte scoring exist.
5. Measure any JS rule change on the main PC/nightly; do not tune on the blind JS sets.
caveats: This is a rule-text and results review, not a scan: the gap list is a research hypothesis list, not measured false alarms.
The JS rules were tuned on OWASP/NodeGoat/vulnerable-node and the 30 apps; the blind sets are spent and the held-out JS snippets are measured, never tuned on.
The current background run is only the tests/test_detection.py subset for the separate Flask .jinja change; it says nothing about JS.
The front-end DOM/XSS inventory (benchmarks/frontend-dom-xss-2026-11-03.json) covers React/jQuery/Svelte/Vue in more detail and should be read with this file.
